conflicts.description: The same real-world concept (an audiovisual work / motion picture) is named 'title_basics' in IMDb and 'film' in Sakila. The word 'title' is also overloaded in IMDb (title_basics.primarytitle, title_akas.title).
conflicts.resolution: Both entities are unified into a single resource named 'title'; the term 'title' is reserved for the work entity, its display name is renamed 'primary_title', and alternative-titles are renamed 'alternative_title'.

conflicts.description: The person entity is named 'name_basics' in IMDb and 'actor' in Sakila, though both represent individuals involved in productions.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a single resource named 'person'.

conflicts.description: Homonym: 'category' denotes the job/role of a credited person in IMDb, but a film genre lookup table in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: The IMDb concept is kept as the 'category' (role) column of 'title_credit'; the Sakila lookup is renamed and modeled as the 'genre' resource.

conflicts.description: Generic name columns ('name', 'city', 'country') are used to store the descriptive label of different lookups, causing name collisions across dimensions.
conflicts.resolution: Renamed to explicit, entity-qualified names: genre_name, language_name, city_name, country_name.

conflicts.description: The column name 'title' refers to four different things: the primary title, the localized alternative title, and (twice) the film title in two Sakila tables.
conflicts.resolution: Disambiguated into 'primary_title' (unified IMDb primarytitle + Sakila film/title_text title) and 'alternative_title' (IMDb title_akas title).

conflicts.description: The language concept is represented as an inline string column in IMDb and as an independent lookup table in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as a shared 'language' dimension; IMDb's per-alt-title language is captured via a language_id foreign key.

conflicts.description: 'film_text' duplicates the film title and description under a different name.
conflicts.resolution: Recognized as a denormalized copy of 'film'; merged into 'title' and not materialized as a separate resource.

conflicts.description: 'region' (IMDb) and 'country' (Sakila) both denominate geographic areas but with different labelling and granularity.
conflicts.resolution: Kept distinct: 'region' remains a title-distribution attribute on 'title_alternative'; 'country' is modeled as a normalized dimension.

conflicts.description: IMDb identifier columns are declared as 'number' although their descriptions state they are alphanumeric strings (e.g. 'tt0000001', 'nm0000001').
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'string' across all target resources.

conflicts.description: Year values are declared as 'string' (YYYY) in IMDb and as 'string' in Sakila even though they are numeric.
conflicts.resolution: Standardized to 'integer' (birth_year, death_year, release_year, end_year).

conflicts.description: Declared as 'integer' although the description states it is the primary title string.
conflicts.resolution: Corrected to 'string' (primary_title).

conflicts.description: Sakila foreign-key columns are typed inconsistently: some 'integer' (film.language_id, address.city_id, inventory.film_id) while the referenced primary keys are 'string'.
conflicts.resolution: All identifier and foreign-key columns are uniformly typed as 'string'.

conflicts.description: Numeric measurements and money values are stored as 'string' in Sakila.
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'integer' (rental_duration_days) and 'number' (rental_rate, replacement_cost, amount, runtime_minutes).

conflicts.description: Boolean flags are inconsistently typed: 'string' in Sakila (active) versus 'boolean' in IMDb (isadult, isoriginaltitle), and encoded as 0/1 in IMDb.
conflicts.resolution: All flags are typed 'boolean' (active, is_adult, is_original_title).

conflicts.description: Columns described as 'date and time' are typed 'date', losing the time component.
conflicts.resolution: Re-typed to 'datetime'.

conflicts.description: Sakila surrogate keys are declared as 'string' although they are integer surrogates, whereas IMDb uses alphanumeric natural keys.
conflicts.resolution: Uniformly typed 'string' to allow the merged keys of both sources to co-exist.

conflicts.description: Two different notions of 'rating': IMDb is a continuous weighted average (0-10), Sakila is a categorical age/MPAA rating (G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17). Different scale and encoding.
conflicts.resolution: Kept as separate semantics: 'average_rating' (number) in the title_rating resource and 'content_rating' (string) on 'title'.

conflicts.description: Both express the runtime, and both use minutes as the unit; Sakila's column is however typed as string and unlabelled.
conflicts.resolution: Aligned on the common SI-friendly unit of minutes into a single 'runtime_minutes' integer column.

conflicts.description: IMDb encodes missing values with the literal '\N' inside year strings, which is a value-level encoding not representable once years become integers.
conflicts.resolution: The '\N' sentinel is normalized to a null value when casting years to integer.

conflicts.description: Same concept (language) encoded differently: IMDb uses ISO-like codes, Sakila uses English language names.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into a 'language' dimension; IMDb codes are harmonized to the dimension's identity while its name attribute carries the English label.

conflicts.description: Genre/category vocabularies differ between sources (IMDb's fixed genre set vs Sakila's rental-shop categories), and IMDb limits a title to three genres.
conflicts.resolution: Both are mapped into a single 'genre' dimension and a shared 'title_genre' bridge; vocabulary harmonization is left to a controlled value list.

conflicts.description: Active flags are documented to be set to 'FALSE' (rather than deleting rows), implying string/boolean ambiguity in encoding.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized to a real boolean type with a uniform true/false semantics.

conflicts.description: Geographic scope is represented at different granularities (distribution region, country dimension, and free-text district).
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as separate attributes at the correct granularity rather than forcing a lossy merge.

conflicts.description: IMDb stores many-to-many data as delimited/array values packed into a single column, whereas Sakila stores the same kinds of associations in fully normalized bridge tables.
conflicts.resolution: IMDb arrays are decomposed into bridge/child resources (title_genre, title_credit, person_profession, person_known_for) consistent with the normalized Sakila pattern; free-text arrays that are non-enumerated (attributes, types, characters) remain delimited strings.

conflicts.description: film_text is a denormalized projection of the film table (title + description keyed by film_id), introducing redundancy.
conflicts.resolution: Dropped as a separate resource; its columns are folded into 'title' with provenance retained.

conflicts.description: IMDb splits the title/person relationship across two tables of differing shape: title_crew packs director and writer arrays into one row per title, while title_principals holds one row per person credit.
conflicts.resolution: Both are unpivoted and unified into the row-per-credit 'title_credit' resource alongside Sakila's film_actor.

conflicts.description: Sakila has a normalized three-level location hierarchy that has no counterpart in IMDb.
conflicts.resolution: Preserved as separate country, city, and address resources, with foreign keys maintaining the hierarchy.

conflicts.description: IMDb models the series/episode relationship as a self-referencing association within a title-oriented table, unlike the flat Sakila model.
conflicts.resolution: Extracted into a dedicated 'title_episode' child resource with a self-referencing foreign key to 'title'.

conflicts.description: Sakila contains a complete rental/commerce domain (inventory, rental, payment, store, staff, customer) with no counterpart in IMDb.
conflicts.resolution: Retained as-is (normalized to the unified 'title' foreign key where it referenced 'film'), as these are legitimate domain-specific resources.

conflicts.description: The title-to-ratings relationship is 1:1 (a single ratings row per title), whereas most other audio-visual relationships are 1:N or N:M.
conflicts.resolution: Modeled as a 1:1 extension resource 'title_rating' whose primary key is the title_id foreign key.

conflicts.description: Person-to-title is N:M in both sources but is expressed through different mechanisms and role semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into the N:M 'title_credit' bridge between 'person' and 'title'.

conflicts.description: Sakila title-to-genre is a clean N:M bridge; IMDb embeds an inline array of up to three genres per title.
conflicts.resolution: Unified into the N:M 'title_genre' bridge.

conflicts.description: A TV series relates 1:N to its episodes, and each episode maps back to exactly one parent series.
conflicts.resolution: Represented via self-referencing foreign keys on 'title_episode'.

conflicts.description: Circular 1:N references between store and staff (a store has a manager staff member; a staff member belongs to a home store).
conflicts.resolution: Both foreign keys are retained in the unified schema; the cycle is preserved as-is.

conflicts.description: The 'known for' relationship is 1:N from a person to several titles in IMDb.
conflicts.resolution: Normalized into the 'person_known_for' resource linking person to title.

conflicts.description: title_akas declares no primary key, although the pair (titleid, ordering) is the natural unique identifier.
conflicts.resolution: Adopted the composite natural key (title_id, ordering) as the primary key of 'title_alternative'.

conflicts.description: Several IMDb tables declare no primary key at all, despite having natural keys (tconst, or tconst+ordering).
conflicts.resolution: Natural keys are inferred: title_episode and title_rating use title_id; title_credit uses a synthetic surrogate key because its natural key spans unpivoted sources.

conflicts.description: Primary-key conventions differ: IMDb uses alphanumeric natural keys (typed as number) while Sakila uses integer surrogate keys (typed as string).
conflicts.resolution: Both key styles are unified as 'string' identifiers, and merged entities reuse them (title_id, person_id).

conflicts.description: Sakila bridge tables declare no primary key even though (film_id, actor_id) and (film_id, category_id) are unique.
conflicts.resolution: Composite primary keys are declared on the corresponding bridge resources (title_genre; title_credit exposed via a surrogate key).

conflicts.description: payment declares payment_id but does not mark it as the primary key, while rental does mark rental_id.
conflicts.resolution: payment_id is adopted as the primary key of 'payment'.

conflicts.description: Merging entities from two independent sources produces several source primary keys feeding one target key.
conflicts.resolution: The unified 'person' and 'title' primary keys list all contributing source primary keys in their provenance.
